cells.tense: The pen is in your hand and the direction is already moving through you.
cells.ask: Take one thing you've been circling and say the next step out loud to one person, then take it — this week.
cells.core:
You get a direction going and it moves. Not frantic — you pick a line and the energy keeps traveling down it, even when the road pushes back. People can tell when you mean it, and the thing gathers weight because you're standing behind it.

What you're working with hasn't asked for much: follow the current to the next real decision and let it be seen. Pick the one you keep circling and take the next step where someone can see you take it. That's the whole ask. What it feeds is more of your own motion coming back to you with proof attached.
cells.sheetLine: You pick a direction and the energy keeps traveling down it.
cells.verb: starting things with a confidence that shows
cells.place: somewhere with a direction to keep

cells.tense: You are already out past the next bend, living in a result that has not arrived.
cells.ask: Ask one question you don't already know the answer to, and let the answer land before you move again.
cells.core:
You're ahead of the thing itself. Somewhere out front is the version where it works, and you're spending today defending it — starting, restarting, lighting one more fire before the last one has caught. The push is real. It is also using the fuel that was meant for the walk.

Try it from the other end: ask one question you don't already answer, and wait for what comes back. You don't have to drop the direction. Just let one piece of the world get here before you move. The shine you're after comes from what's actually finished, not from how hard the next start is.
cells.sheetLine: You're starting fires faster than any of them can catch.
cells.verb: starting things with a confidence that shows
cells.place: somewhere with a direction to keep

cells.tense: A door you already stepped through is still the one you're standing at.
cells.ask: Find one small thing you could grow this week and tend it — check on it, learn what it needs, keep it alive.
cells.core:
A direction you set down is still a live line — you know the next step and the energy carries you to it. The confidence isn't loud; it's the plain fact that what you mean to do and what you do are the same thing. That is the shape of it when the starting is working.

The starting has gone quiet for you. You're beside a door you already walked through, holding a direction you haven't picked up, and the stillness has begun to feel like your actual size. Don't try to relight the old fire. Grow something small instead — one living thing or one plain project — and let it tell you what it needs. Tending refills the same muscle that carries a direction, and the charge comes back through doing, not deciding.
cells.sheetLine: Nothing's moving because nothing's being started.

cells.tense: The motion is already running and you are calling it the situation.
cells.ask: Pick one direction you're already carrying and say out loud that you chose it — then keep going.
cells.core:
This one looks ordinary when it's working: you decide, keep a line through the week, and the momentum is there because you are behind it. Nobody announces that. It just shows up as the person who knows where things are going.

And you are that one — moving the thing, keeping the direction steady — except it doesn't get filed under your name. It gets called the job, the momentum, how things go. Stand inside what's already true. One direction you're carrying: say that you picked it. The strength was there before you said so, and saying it doesn't add effort — it makes what you're carrying yours to keep. Nothing about the direction has to change for that.
cells.sheetLine: You're already the one steering this. Say so.
